snippet.title: 10 Paint Correction Mistakes Beginners Make And How to Avoid Them
snippet.description:
If your paint still looks bad after polishing, you’re probably making one of these common paint correction mistakes. In this video, I break down the 10 biggest mistakes beginners make - and how to avoid them for better results.

Paint correction can completely transform your car’s appearance - but only if it’s done properly. If you’re not getting the results you expected, chances are you’re making one (or more) of these common mistakes.

In this video, I walk you through 10 paint correction mistakes beginners make, explain why your paint may still look bad after polishing, and show you how to fix these issues step by step.

You’ll learn:
✔ Why a 1-step correction won’t remove all defects
✔ How to choose the right pad and polish combo
✔ Why proper lighting is critical to see real results
✔ The importance of using a panel prep to remove polishing oils
✔ Why washing and decontamination alone won’t remove old protection
✔ When paint correction becomes too aggressive (and risky)
✔ How to maintain your results so you don’t have to polish again for years

One of the biggest myths in car detailing is that strong soaps or decontamination products can fully remove existing protection like ceramic coatings. In reality, the only way to ensure 100% removal is through proper paint correction using machine polishing and mechanical abrasion.

Whether you’re a beginner or an enthusiast, this video will help you achieve better results, avoid costly mistakes, and protect your vehicle’s paint for the long term.
